ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
In the final of the 2000m mixed team relay in short track speed skating at the Winter Olympics.

1. Assuming the athlete's motion before entering the curve after the start is a uniformly accelerated rectilinear motion with an initial velocity of zero, if the athlete accelerates to a velocity of $v=9\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}$ after covering a distance of $x=15\mathrm{m}$, determine the magnitude of the acceleration.
2. Assuming the athlete's motion in the curve is a uniform circular motion along a semicircular track, as shown in the figure, if athletes A and B enter the curve simultaneously with radii of $R_{A}=8\mathrm{m}$ and $R_{B}=9\mathrm{m}$, and speeds of $v_{A}=10\mathrm{m/s}$ and $v_{B}=11\mathrm{m/s}$ respectively, determine the ratio of their centripetal accelerations and, through calculation, identify which athlete will exit the curve first.

ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: In the final of the 2000m mixed team relay in short track speed skating at the Winter Olympics. 1. Assuming the athlete's motion before entering the curve after the start is uniformly accelerated rectilinear motion with an initial velocity of zero, if the athlete accelerates to a velocity of $v=9\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}$ after covering a distance of $x=15\mathrm{m}$, determine the magnitude of the acceleration. 2. Assuming the athlete's motion in the curve is uniform circular motion along a semicircular track, as shown in the figure, if athletes A and B enter the curve simultaneously with radii of $R_A=8\mathrm{m}$ and $R_B=9\mathrm{m}$, and speeds of $v_A=10\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}$ and $v_B=11\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}$ respectively, determine the ratio of their centripetal accelerations and, through calculation, identify which athlete will exit the curve first.
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure shows concentric semicircular bends with the black dot on the left as the center; the dashed lines represent semicircular trajectories of different radii; the arrows indicate the radius R_A of the more inner trajectory where athlete A is located, and the radius R_B of the more outer trajectory where athlete B is located. The two people move along the semicircular bend, and it is necessary to compare their respective centripetal accelerations and the time required to pass through the semicircular arc. Reasoning: 1. After starting, before entering the bend, they do uniformly accelerated linear motion with initial velocity 0. It is known that v_0=0, v=9 m/s, x=15 m. From v^2-v_0^2=2ax, get a=(9^2-0)/(2×15)=81/30=2.7 m/s^2. 2. In the bend, they do uniform circular motion, and the centripetal acceleration a_c=v^2/R. A's centripetal acceleration a_A=10^2/8=100/8; B's centripetal acceleration a_B=11^2/9=121/9. Therefore a_A/a_B=(100/8)/(121/9)=225/242. The semicircular arc length is πR, so the time to pass through the bend is t_A=πR_A/v_A=8π/10, t_B=πR_B/v_B=9π/11. Comparing gives 8π/10=0.8π, 9π/11≈0.818π, therefore t_A<t_B, and A exits the bend first.
